description: Numbers to call for help, and the rights every citizen has
simple: In any emergency, call 112. Below are {helplines} helplines, grouped by what you need, and {rights} rights every citizen has. Tap a number to call it.
tileRightsSub: Tap one to learn how to use it
helplinesLead: Tap a card to call. Tap ⓘ to see when to call and what to say.
rightsLead: Rights you have by law, in plain words. Tap a card to see how to use it.
sayEmergency: Say where you are (a landmark helps), what happened, and how many people need help. Stay on the line.
sayOther: Keep your name, your place and any reference number ready, and write down the complaint number they give you.
checkNote: These are national numbers. Some states also run their own lines; your district office can tell you which work best where you live.

national.name: National emergency
national.when: Any emergency: police, fire or ambulance. One number for all of them.

police.name: Police emergency
police.when: A crime is happening, someone is in danger, or you need the police fast.

ambulance.name: Ambulance
ambulance.when: A medical emergency: an accident, chest pain, a difficult birth, a snake bite.

fire.name: Fire
fire.when: A fire, a gas leak, or someone trapped in a building.

road.name: Road accident
road.when: To report a road accident and get help to the spot.

women.name: Women helpline
women.when: A woman or girl is harassed, threatened or unsafe, at home or outside.

child.name: Child helpline
child.when: A child is lost, hurt, made to work, being married off, or in any danger.

senior.name: Senior citizens
senior.when: An older person needs help: pension, abuse, loneliness or legal questions.

cyber.name: Cyber crime
cyber.when: Money was stolen online or through UPI. Call at once: the sooner you call, the better the chance to stop the money.

corruption.name: Anti-corruption
corruption.when: An official asks you for a bribe.

consumer.name: Consumer helpline
consumer.when: A complaint about something you bought: a faulty product, overcharging, or a bad service.

pmkisan.name: PM-KISAN helpline
pmkisan.when: Questions about PM-KISAN payments to farmers.

rti.title: Right to Information (RTI)
rti.desc: Any citizen can ask for government information. The office must reply within 30 days. Fee: ₹10.
rti.more: Under the Right to Information Act, you can ask any government office for copies of its records, files and decisions. You do not have to say why you want them.
rti.step1: Write your question clearly: what you want, for which period, from which office.
rti.step2: Send it to the office's Public Information Officer, online or by post, with the ₹10 fee. People below the poverty line pay no fee.
rti.step3: No reply in 30 days, or a poor reply? File a first appeal with the same office.

food.title: Right to Food
food.desc: Families with a ration card under the National Food Security Act (NFSA) get food grain free every month: 5 kg per person, or 35 kg for an Antyodaya family.
food.more: Under the National Food Security Act, families with a ration card (priority household or Antyodaya) get food grain from the ration shop every month.
food.step1: Apply for a ration card at your food and civil supplies office, or on its website.
food.step2: Collect your grain at the ration shop every month. With One Nation One Ration Card, your card works at any ration shop in India.
food.step3: Refused, or given less? Complain to the food department's helpline or the district supply officer.

education.title: Right to Education
education.desc: Free and compulsory schooling for every child aged 6 to 14, under the RTE Act.
education.more: Under the RTE Act, every child aged 6 to 14 can study free in a nearby government school. Private schools must keep a quarter of their entry-class seats free for children from poorer families.
education.step1: Enrol your child in the nearest government school. No fee and no entrance test are allowed.
education.step2: For the free seats in private schools, apply on your state's RTE admission portal when it opens.
education.step3: Refused admission, or asked for money? Complain to the Block Education Officer.
education.law: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009

mgnrega.title: MGNREGA (work guarantee)
mgnrega.desc: 100 days of guaranteed paid work a year for every rural household that asks for it.
mgnrega.more: Every rural household can ask for up to 100 days of paid work a year. If work is not given within 15 days, you are owed an unemployment allowance.
mgnrega.step1: Get a job card from your gram panchayat. It is free.
mgnrega.step2: Ask for work in writing, and keep the dated receipt.
mgnrega.step3: Wages must reach your bank account within 15 days. If they are late, you are owed extra money for the delay.
mgnrega.law: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005

gramSabha.title: Gram Sabha
gramSabha.desc: Go to your village's Gram Sabha meetings. Every adult voter of the village can take part.
gramSabha.more: The Gram Sabha is the meeting of all adult voters of the village panchayat. It approves the village plan, picks who gets scheme benefits, and checks the panchayat's spending.
gramSabha.step1: Ask your panchayat office when the next Gram Sabha is. It must meet a few times every year.
gramSabha.step2: Go, and ask about works and spending. You can ask to see the accounts.
gramSabha.step3: Help choose the families who should get scheme benefits.
gramSabha.law: Your state's Panchayat Raj Act (73rd Amendment to the Constitution)

ward.title: Ward committee
ward.desc: Take part in your ward committee meetings, run by your city corporation.
ward.more: In cities, ward committees let people raise local problems and check local works. How they work depends on your state's city law.
ward.step1: Ask your ward office or councillor when the ward committee meets.
ward.step2: Go with your problem written down: roads, drains, garbage, street lights.
ward.step3: Ask for the ward's list of works and what was spent on them.
ward.law: Your state's municipal law (74th Amendment to the Constitution)

wardBody.title: Ward committee
wardBody.desc: Take part in your ward committee meetings, run by your city corporation ({body}).
wardBody.more: In cities, ward committees let people raise local problems and check local works. Here they are run by {body}.
wardBody.step1: Ask your ward office or councillor when the ward committee meets.
wardBody.step2: Go with your problem written down: roads, drains, garbage, street lights.
wardBody.step3: Ask for the ward's list of works and what was spent on them.
wardBody.law: Your state's municipal law (74th Amendment to the Constitution)

consumer.title: Consumer rights
consumer.desc: File a consumer complaint online at consumerhelpline.gov.in.
consumer.more: You are protected against faulty goods, poor service, overcharging and false adverts. You can complain online, and you do not need a lawyer for small cases.
consumer.step1: Keep the bill, the warranty and any messages with the seller.
consumer.step2: Complain to the seller first. No answer? Call 1915 or 1800-11-4000, or complain at consumerhelpline.gov.in.
consumer.step3: Still not solved? File a case at the District Consumer Commission, online at e-daakhil.nic.in.

rightsNote: This is a short, plain guide, not legal advice. Rules can differ a little from state to state.
